ideas: Better quality products often last longer
Your money supports better companies and practices
Price limits: only for things you use often

phrases.meaning: good enough to justify paying more
over a long period of time
spend less when counting many months
show opinions through what you buy

model: Yes, I'd pay more for eco-friendly products, as long as the difference isn't huge. First, I think they're often worth the extra cost in the long run. For example, I bought a steel water bottle for about three hundred thousand dong, which felt expensive at first. But I haven't bought bottled water for over a year, so I've actually managed to save money over time. If I bought cheap plastic bottles every day, I'd spend much more. Another reason is that I like to vote with my wallet. If more customers choose sustainable brands, other companies will notice and change the way they make things. Last year I switched to a local coffee shop that uses paper cups and sells refills, and it's always busy, so clearly lots of people feel the same. Of course, if I were on a tight budget, I might not be able to do this for everything. But when I can, I try to make a conscious choice. So, overall, yes, paying a little more is worth it.
